questions.q: The value of ${∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2x^{3} - 3x^{2} - x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

Using $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{2a}f\left(x\right)dx = 0$ when$f\left(2a - x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

Now, finding $f\left(1 - x\right)$ we get,

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2{\left(1 - x\right)}^{3} - 3{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2} - \left(1 - x\right) + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2\left(1 - x^{3} - 3x + 3x^{2}\right) - 3{\left(1 + x^{2} - 2x\right)}^{2} - \left(1 - x\right) + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(2 - 2x^{3} - 6x + 6x^{2} - 3 - 3x^{2} + 6x - 1 + x + 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(- 2x^{3} + 3x^{2} + x - 1\right)\dfrac{1}{3}dx$

$⇒ I = - I$

$⇒ f\left(1 - x\right) = - f\left(x\right)$

$∴ I = 0$

questions.q: If $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\cos^{4}xdx = a\pi + b\sqrt{3}$, where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers, then $9a + 8b$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $I = {∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\cos^{4}x d x$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(2\cos^{2}x\right)2 d x$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(1 + \cos 2x\right)2 d x$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(1 + \cos^{2}2x + 2\cos 2x\right) d x$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(1 + 2\cos 2x\right) d x + \dfrac{1}{8}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}2\cos^{2}2xdx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(1 + 2\cos 2x\right) d x + \dfrac{1}{8}{∫}_{0}^{\pi3}\left(1 + \cos 4x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {\dfrac{1}{4}\left(x + \sin 2x\right) + \dfrac{1}{8}\left(x + \dfrac{\sin 4x}{4}\right)}_{0}^{\pi3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{π}{3} + sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right) + \dfrac{1}{8} \left(\dfrac{π}{3} + \dfrac{sin\dfrac{4\pi}{3}}{4}\right)

$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{π}{12} + \dfrac{3}{8}\right) + \left(\dfrac{π}{24} - \dfrac{3}{64}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{8} + \dfrac{7\sqrt{3}}{64}$

So, on comparing with given value we get, $a = \dfrac{1}{8}, b = \dfrac{7}{64}$

$⇒ 9a + 8b = \dfrac{9}{8} + \dfrac{7}{8}$

$⇒ 9a + 8b = \dfrac{16}{8}$

$⇒ 9a + 8b = 2$

$

questions.q: The value of the integral ${∫}_{- \dfrac{π}{4}}^{\pi4}\dfrac{x + \dfrac{π}{4}}{2 - \cos 2x}dx$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let,

$I = {∫}_{- \pi4}^{\pi4}\dfrac{x + \dfrac{π}{4}}{2 - \cos 2x}dx \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now replacing~$x \to - x$~we get,

$⇒ I = {∫}_{- \pi4}^{\$pi4}\dfrac{-x + \dfrac{π}{4}}{2 - \cos 2x}$dx \ldots \left($2\right)$

Now both the equation we get,

$⇒ 2I = {∫}_{- \pi4}^{\pi4}\dfrac{\pi2}{2 - \cos 2x}dx$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{4} \cdot2{∫}_{0}^{\$pi4}\dfrac{dx}{2 - c$\cos 2x}dx \left\${\ttext{as}\cos 2x\text{is even function}\right\}$

$⇒ I = $\dfrac{π}{4} \cdot$2{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\dfrac{\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right)dx}{2\left(1 + \tan^{2}x\right) - \left(1 - \tan^{2}x\right)}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{4} \cdot2{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\dfrac{\sec^{2}\text{ xdx }}${3\tan^{2}x + 1}

Now let~$\tan x = t ⇒ \sec^{2}xdx = dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{dt}{3t^{2} + 1}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{3}}\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi2}{6\sqrt{3}}$

$

questions.q: If  \left[x\right]$ is the greatest integer $\le x,$~then ${π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}\left(sin\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)[ x ]dx$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,& $I = {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)[ x ]dx$

$I = {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)[ x ]dx + {π}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - \left[x\right]\right)[ x ]dx$

$I = {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)x^{0}dx + {π}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - 1\right)1dx$

$I = {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {π}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\left(x - 1\right)dx$

$I = {π}^{2}{∫}_{0}^{1}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx + {π}^{2}\left[x{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right) d x - {∫}_{1}^{2}\left\{\dfrac{d}{dx}x{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right\}dx\right] - {π}^{2}{∫}_{1}^{2}\sin \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx$

$I = {π}^{2}{- \dfrac{2}{π}\cos \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)}_{0}^{1} + {π}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{π}\right \left(- \cos \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left- {∫}_{1}^{2}\dfrac{2}{π}\left(- cos\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)dx\right] + {π}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{π}{\cos \left(\dfrac{πx}{2}\right)}_{1}^{2}$

$I = {π}^{2}{- \dfrac{2}{π}\cos \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)}_{0}^{1} + {π}^{2}{\left[\left(x\right)\dfrac{2}{π}\right \left(- \cos \left(\dfrac{\pix}{2}\right)\right)}_{1}^{2}\left+ \left(\dfrac{2}{π}\right)2{\sin \left(\dfrac{πx}{2}\right)}_{1}^{2}\right] + {π}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{π}{\cos \left(\dfrac{πx}{2}\right)}_{1}^{2}$

$I = - {π}^{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{π}\cos \left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) - \dfrac{2}{π}\cos \left(0\right)\right] + {π}^{2}\left[2 \times \dfrac{2}{π}\left(- cos\pi\right) + 1 \times \dfrac{2}{π} \times \left(cos\dfrac{π}{2}\right)\right]\left+ 4\left[\sin \left(\pi\right) - sin\dfrac{π}{2}\right]\right] + {π}^{2} \times \dfrac{2}{π} \left[\cos \left(\pi\right) -cos\dfrac{π}{2}\right]

$I = $2\pi +4\pi +$4 ( 0 - 1 ) - $2\pi

$I = $4\pi -$4$

$I = 4 \left(\pi -$1\right)

$

Adding \left(i\right)$ and \left(ii\right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \times2{∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\d$dfrac{dx}{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(\sin^{4}x + \cos^{4}x - \sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x\right)}

$\mathop{= ∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\d$dfrac{dx}{\left(\sin^{2}x + \cos^{2}x\right)2 - 3\sin^{2}x\cos^{2}x} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{dx}{1 - $\dfrac{3}{4}\sin^{2}$2x}$


$= {∫}_{0}^{\$pi2}\dfrac{4\sec^{2}2xdx}{4\left(1 + \tan^{2}2x\right) - 3\tan^{2}2x} =2{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\dfrac{4\sec^{2}2x}{4 + \tan^{2}2x}$dx$

Let~$\tan 2x = t$ and $2\sec^{2}2xdx = dt$

$I = 4\mathop{∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{dt}{{2}^{2} + t^{2}} = $\dfrac{4}{2}{\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{t}{2}}_{0}^{∞}$~=2\left(\dfrac{π}{2} -0\right) = $\pi

questions.q: The integral $\int_{-1}^{\frac{3}{2}}\left(\left|\pi^2 x \sin (\pi x)\right|\right) d x$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $\mathrm{I}=\pi^2 \int_{-1}^{3 / 2}|\mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{x}| \mathrm{dx}$
$\begin{aligned}
& =\pi^2\left\{\int_{-1}^1 \mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{xdx}-\int_1^{3 / 2} \mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{xdx}\right\} \\ & =\pi^2\left\{2 \int_0^1 \mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{xdx}-\int_{-1}^{3 / 2} \mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{xdx}\right\}
\end{aligned}$
Consider
$\begin{aligned}
& \int \mathrm{x} \sin \pi \mathrm{xdx} \\ & -\mathrm{x} \cdot \frac{1}{\pi} \cos \pi \mathrm{x}+\int 1 \cdot \frac{1}{\pi} \cos \pi \mathrm{xdx} \\ & =-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\pi} \cos \pi \mathrm{x}+\frac{\sin \pi \mathrm{x}}{\pi^2}
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{I} & =\pi^2\left\{2\left(-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\pi} \cos \pi \mathrm{x}+\frac{\sin \pi \mathrm{x}}{\pi^2}\right)_0^1-\left(-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\pi} \cos \pi \mathrm{x}+\frac{\sin \pi \mathrm{x}}{\pi^2}\right)_1^{3 / 2}\right\} \\ & =\pi^2\left\{\frac{2}{\pi}-\left(-\frac{1}{\pi^2}-\frac{1}{\pi}\right)\right\} \\ & =\pi^2\left\{\frac{3}{\pi}+\frac{1}{\pi^2}\right\} \\ & =3 \pi+1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the integral $\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\dfrac{xdx}{\sin^{4}\left(2x\right) + \cos^{4}\left(2x\right)}$ equals:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let, $\mathop{I = ∫}_{0}^{\pi4}\dfrac{xdx}{\sin^{4}\left(2x\right) + \cos^{4}\left(2x\right)}$

Let, $2x = t$ then $dx = \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{tdt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{π}{2} - t\right)dt}{\sin^{4}\left(\dfrac{π}{2} - t\right) + \cos^{4}\left(\dfrac{π}{2} - t\right)}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\dfrac{π}{2}dt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t} - I$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{π}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{dt}{\sin^{4}t + \cos^{4}t}$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{π}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{\pi2}\dfrac{\sec^{4}tdt}{\tan^{4}t + 1}$

Let, $\tan t = y$ then $\sec^{2}tdt = dy$

$⇒ 2I = \dfrac{π}{8}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{\left(1 + y^{2}\right)dy}{1 + y^{4}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{16}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{∞}\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{y2}}{y^{2} + \dfrac{1}{y2}}dy$

Putting, $y - \dfrac{1}{y} = p$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{16}\mathop{∫}_{- \infty}^{∞}\dfrac{dp}{p^{2} + \left(\sqrt{2}\right)2}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{π}{16\sqrt{2}}{\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{p}{2}\right)}_{- \infty}^{∞}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\pi2}{16\sqrt{2}}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}{π}^{2}}{32}$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{- $\pi$/ 2}^{- $1}\left(\left[-$2 - \sin x\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{- $1}^{0}\left(\left[-$1 - \sin x\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\left[$0 - \sin x\right]\right)dx + {∫}_{1}^{\pi2}\left(\left[1 - \sin x\right]\right)dx$

$⇒ I = - 2{∫}_{- \pi/ 2}^{- 1}dx - {∫}_{- 1}^{0}dx - 1{∫}_{0}^{1}dx + {∫}_{1}^{\pi2}0 \cdotdx$

$⇒ I = - 2\left(-1 + $\dfrac{π}{2}\right) -$1 - 1$

$⇒ I = - \pi$

$

questions.solution:
$Let $I = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)g\left(x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(a - x\right)g\left(a - x\right)dx$~ ~ (Using properties of definite integration)

$⇒ I = {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)\left(4 - g\left(x\right)\right)dx \left[∵ f \left($x\right) = f \left(a - x\right) \text{ and } g\left(x\right) + g\left(a - x\right) = 4\right]$

$⇒ I = 4{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\right)dx - {∫}_{0}^{a}f\left(x\$right)g\left($x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 4{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($x\right)dx - I$

$⇒ 2I = 4{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($x\right)dx$

$⇒ I = 2{∫}_{0}^{a}f\left($x\right)dx$

questions.q: Let $f: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ and $F\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}tf  \left($t\right)dt$. If $F\left($x^{2}\right) = x^{4} + x^{5},$ then $\mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left($r^{2}\right)$ is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given:

$F\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x}t ⋅ f\left(t\right)dt$

Now, applying Newton Leibnitz Theorem we get,

$F^{'} \left(x\right) = x ⋅ f \left($x\right)$

And F\left($x^{2}\right) = x^{4} + x^{5}$

Let $x^{2} = t$

$⇒ $F\left($t\right) = t^{2} + $t\dfrac{5}{2}

$⇒ F^{'}\left($t\right) = 2t + $\$ddfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}\left\{\text{as}F^{'}\left(x\right) = x ⋅ f\left(x\right)\right\}$

$⇒ t ⋅ f\left(t\right) = 2t + $\ddfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ $f\left($t\right) = 2 + $\ddfrac{5}{2}t\dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f\left(r^{2}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}2 + \dfrac{5}{2}r$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}^{12}f \left(r^{2}\right) = 24 + $\dfrac{5}{2}\left[\dfrac{12\left(13\right)}{2}\right]$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{r = 1}$^{12}f\left($r^{2}\right) = 219

questions.q: Let& $f$~be a differentiable function defined on~  \left[0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right]$~such~that~$f\left(x\right) > 0$~and~$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f\left(t\right)\sqrt{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(f \left($t\right)\right)\right)2}dt = e$~$\forall  x \in \left[$0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right], then~ \left\{6\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(f\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right)\right\}2& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right) + {∫}_{0}^{x}f \left(t\$right)\sqrt{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left(f\left(t\right)\right)\right)2}$dt = e . . . \left($1\right)$

Put~$x = 0$, then

$f \left($0\right) = e$.

Differentiating~\left($1\right)$~w.r.t.~$x$, we get

$f^{'} \left(x\right) + f \left(x\$right)\sqrt{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left($f \left(x\right)\right)\right)2}$ =0$

Put~$y = f\left(x\right)$.

\dfrac{dy}{dx} ++y\sqrt{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}y\right)2} =0$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y\sqrt{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}y\right)2}} = -∫ dx$

$⇒ ∫ \dfrac{d\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}y\right)}{1 - \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}y\right)2} = -∫ dx$

$⇒ \sin^{- 1}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}y\right) = - x + C$

Put~$x = 0, y = e$

$\sin^{- 1}\left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}e\right) = - 0 + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{π}{2}$

So,

$\sin^{- 1} \left(\log_{\mathrm{e}}$y\right) = - x + $\dfrac{π}{2}

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}y = $sin \left(-$x + \dfrac{π}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}f \left($x\right) = sin \left(-x + $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)

Put~$x = $\dfrac{π}{6}

$⇒ \log_{\mathrm{e}}f\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) ==sin\left(- \dfrac{π}{6} + \dfrac{π}{2}\right) ==sin\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}

$⇒ $6\log_{\mathrm{e}}f \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) ==3\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \left$\${6\log_{\mathrm{e}}f\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)\right\}$2 = 27$
